definitions.explanation: A streak of light in the night sky caused by a small piece of space debris burning up as it enters Earth's atmosphere.

examples.japanese: {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}を{見|み}たら{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}をする。
examples.english: If you see a shooting star, make a wish.

examples.japanese: {昨夜|さくや}、{流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}が{空|そら}を{横切|よこぎ}るのを{見|み}た。
examples.english: Last night, I saw a shooting star streak across the sky.

examples.japanese: {流星群|りゅうせいぐん}の{夜|よる}は{流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}がたくさん{見|み}える。
examples.english: On nights of meteor showers, you can see many shooting stars.

notes:
{流|なが}れ{星|ぼし} refers to shooting stars or meteors. {流|なが}れ means 'flowing' and {星|ぼし} means 'star.'

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}を{見|み}る: to see a shooting star
- {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}に{願|ねが}いをかける: to make a wish on a shooting star
- {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}が{流|なが}れる: a shooting star falls

METEOR SHOWERS ({流星群|りゅうせいぐん}):
- ペルセウス{座|ざ}{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}: Perseids (August)
- ふたご{座|ざ}{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}: Geminids (December)
- しぶんぎ{座|ざ}{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}: Quadrantids (January)

SCIENTIFIC TERMS:
- {流星|りゅうせい}: meteor (scientific)
- {隕石|いんせき}: meteorite (if it reaches ground)

CULTURAL NOTE:
- In Japan, it's believed that if you make a wish before a shooting star disappears, it will come true
